title: Electrical Infrastructure Safety
summary: Learn the boundary between classroom electrical reasoning and licensed electrical work.
objectives: Classify safe classroom and prohibited electrical actions.
Explain why permission, PPE, and escalation matter.

vocab.def: Connected to a source of electrical energy.
Passing a concern to an authorized person or team.

sections.heading: Safety is the first system
sections.body: Diagrams, formulas, simulations, and approved low-voltage educational equipment may support learning. Mains panels, exposed conductors, UPS internals, generators, switchgear, and wiring are professional environments only.

sections.heading: Stop and escalate
sections.body: Opening a panel, probing mains voltage, servicing equipment, or executing professional lockout/tagout is not a Grade 11 classroom task. Stopping and escalating is the correct decision.

practice.prompt: A simulated alarm suggests a panel inspection. What should a student do?
practice.answer: Record the evidence and escalate; do not open or touch the panel.

quiz.question: Which is safe in this course?

lab.objective: Classify electrical actions by safety boundary.

reflectionPrompt: Why can refusing unsafe work be good technical judgment?
